title: Benedict in the cave (c. 500)
hook: a student leaves Rome in disgust and lives three years in a cave at Subiaco

segments.voice: Yesterday, Leo's Christmas sermon: Christian, recognize your dignity. Your line was know your dignity.

A rope comes down a rock face, with a loaf of bread tied to the end and a little bell on it. Below, in a cave in the hills east of Rome, a young man hears the bell, reaches out, and takes his bread. Up above, a monk named Romanus has saved it from his own meals. He does this day after day, for a young man nobody else knows is there. The young man is Benedict. He was supposed to be a student in Rome.
screen: `A ROPE, A LOAF, A BELL.` → `A MONK ABOVE.` → `A YOUNG MAN BELOW.`

segments.voice: Our source is Pope Gregory the Great, who wrote Benedict's life in his Dialogues and says he heard it from Benedict's own disciples. Benedict came from a good family in the region of Nursia, and was sent to Rome to study. There he looked around. Gregory says he saw many of the students sliding into vice, and pulled back the foot he'd just set in the world, afraid that if he took in too much of it, he'd fall in headlong himself. So he left his books, his father's house and his inheritance, wanting to please God alone. Gregory has a phrase worth keeping: Benedict left knowingly ignorant and wisely unlearned. He wasn't running from learning. He was running from a kind of life. Next, the cave. Benedict went to a wild place called Subiaco. On the way he met Romanus, a monk, who gave him the monk's habit and kept his secret. Benedict lived in a narrow cave, Gregory says, for three years, unknown to everyone except Romanus, who lowered bread to him on that rope with its bell. Gregory adds that the devil once threw a stone and broke the bell. Romanus kept feeding him anyway. And here's the twist. Eventually shepherds found him, and at first took him for a wild animal, dressed as he was in skins. But once they talked with him, many of them changed their lives. The hiding place started to become a gathering place. Catholics still visit the cave at Subiaco today, with a monastery built around it.
screen: `A STUDENT IN ROME.` · `KNOWINGLY IGNORANT.` · `THREE YEARS IN A CAVE.` · `THE SHEPHERDS FIND HIM.` · then, large: `AWAY FROM ROME.`

segments.voice: Step away from one noisy thing, the phone in your hand, a room with a television, a group chat that never stops: put the phone face down or in another room, and find a corner, a chair, a car parked somewhere quiet. Let that be your cave, and listen to what's left when the noise is gone. If you pray, use the time the way Benedict did, simply to be with God.
specus. Latin for a cave, the word Gregory used for Benedict's hiding place at Subiaco, fed by a rope and a bell. Today's word.
Your line: away from rome. A little quiet goes a long way. Seven hundred fifty days now.

howItsDone: Catholics honor Saint Benedict as a saint and a founder of monastic life, and pilgrims visit the Sacred Cave at Subiaco, where a monastery now stands around the place he lived.
